Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

obviously adverb

also clearly, evidently, plainly, obvious, it’s obvious that, it’s clear that, apparent

classical

Cic. Phil. 2.84: appāret esse commōtum
Ter. Eun. 485: appāret servum hunc esse dominī pauperis

appāret

impersonal of appāreō, with an accusative and infinitive or a question

it is plain, obviously

Lewis & Short: appāret states what is plain to see; vidētur, what seems so to the speaker (see seem). For “appear, come into sight” see appear.

Other words

  • scīlicet — evidently, of course, naturally

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.2b.1: nōndum scīlicet; Traupman 105

    From scīre licet, “one may know”; often ironic (Lewis & Short; see of course).

  • vidēlicet — evidently, plainly

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 263: errat vidēlicet; Cic. Fin. 2.75: rem vidēlicet difficilem et obscūram!

    From vidēre licet, “one may see”; classical, but much rarer than scīlicet, and ironic too (Lewis & Short).

  • perspicuum est — it is evident (that)

    with an accusative and infinitive · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.342: perspicuum est igitur alia esse in homine optanda, alia laudanda

  • manifestō — palpably, red-handed; Traupman’s “obviously”

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 3.4 (Lewis & Short): manifestō dēprehenderētur; Traupman 353

    Traupman gives it for “obviously” (p. 353); classically it is “palpably”, said above all of someone caught in the act (Plaut., Cic.: Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • nōn dissimulat, patrēs cōnscrīptī: appāret esse commōtum; sūdat, pallet.

    He does not hide it, senators: he is obviously upset; he is sweating, he is pale.Cic. Phil. 2.84

  • Appāret servum hunc esse dominī pauperis

    Obviously this slave belongs to a poor masterTer. Eun. 485

  • ā tē litterās exspectābam, nōndum scīlicet; nam hās māne rescrībēbam.

    I was expecting a letter from you — not yet, obviously, for I am writing this in the morning.Cic. Att. 13.2b.1

See also of course, clearly, appear, seem, certainly.
